jobs.occupation: Maximizing use of fresh grass for dairy cows by combining grazing, zero-grazing, and multispecies swards
jobs.employer_name: Technical Sciences - Institut for Husdyr- og Veter
jobs.description:
Applicants are invited for a PhD fellowship/scholarship at Graduate School of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark, within the Animal and Veterinary Sciences programme. The position is available from 01 March 2027 or later. You can submit your application via the link under 'how to apply'.

Title:
Maximizing use of fresh grass for dairy cows by combining grazing, zero-grazing, and multispecies swards

Research area and project description:
We are seeking a dedicated PhD student for a 3-year position within the topic of dairy production with fresh grass as a main forage source.

The impact of dairy production on environment and climate is of continued importance and interest. Cropping and feeding fresh grass can potentially improve the impact of dairy production on greenhouse gas emissions and nitrogen leakage to surrounding fresh waters.

The project investigates the potential of maximizing fresh grass forage intake to reduce enteric methane emission and increase nitrogen utilization, while maintaining milk production. A series of trials with lactating dairy cows are planned investigating combinations of grazing, zero-grazing, and multispecies swards.

This project offers:
 
• A unique opportunity to contribute to a more sustainable agriculture and environmental-friendly milk production
• An active and stimulating academic environment with several other PhD students and early career staff
• Access to state-of-the-art research facilities for both barn-housing, grazing, and pasture management for dairy cattle
• Collaboration with a range of research partners
• Collaborative projects that foster innovative thinking and practical implementation
Qualifications and specific competences:
Applicants to the PhD position must hold a relevant university degree (MSc) in Animal Science, Agricultural Science, or related fields.

The candidate is expected to have:
 
• Understanding of ruminant nutrition and digestion
• Experience with data handling and analysis using at least one software.
• Ability and interest in collaborating across disciplines with project partners.
• Ability to communicate effectively in English.
• Good scientific and writing skills.
 Place of employment and place of work:
The place of employment is Aarhus University, and the place of work is Department of Animal and Veterinary Sciences, Research center Foulum, Blichers allé 20, 8830 Tjele, Denmark.

Contact:
Applicants seeking further information regarding the PhD position are invited to contact:
• Mogens Larsen, e-mail: Mogens.Larsen@anivet.au.dk (main supervisor)
• Nikolaj P. Hansen, e-mail: Nikolaj.Hansen@anivet.au.dk (co-supervisor)
For information about application requirements and mandatory attachments, please see our application guide. If answers cannot be found there, please contact:
• admission.gradschool.tech@au.dk
How to apply:
Please follow this link to submit your application.

Application deadline is 06 December 2026 at 23:59 CET.
Preferred starting date is 01 March 2027.

For technical reasons, you must upload a project description. Please copy the project description above and upload it as a PDF in the application.

Please note:
• Only documents received prior to the application deadline will be evaluated. Thus, documents sent after deadline will not be considered.
• The programme committee may request further information or invite the applicant to attend an interview.
• Shortlisting will be used, which means that the evaluation committee only will evaluate the most relevant applications.
Formalities and salary range
Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions. You will be employed as an academic staff member at basic salary grades 4–8. As a PhD fellow you will also receive a monthly non-pensionable allowance.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which everyone has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

The application must be submitted via the online recruitment system, which can be accessed under ‘How to apply’.

jobs.occupation: PhD Fellowship in DNA Replication and Genome Stability After Whole-Genome Doubling
jobs.description:
At the laboratory of Associate Professor Kumar Somyajit, we invite applications for a fully funded PhD fellowship investigating how cells adapt the DNA replication machinery when their genome doubles. The project connects a fundamental challenge in development with a common route of cancer evolution. Previous work in the field of cell cycle and genome integrity and experience in working on embryonic/adult stem cells and cancer cell lines are a plus.

The Somyajit lab, based at the Quantitative Cell Biology and Bioimaging research unit at the Department of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology, SDU, has a deep interest in studying regulatory foundations of the cell cycle, DNA replication, and genome surveillance in pathophysiology.
Starting date: 01-01-2027, or as soon as possible thereafter. Duration: 3 years as a PhD Student. Interviews of shortlisted candidates will be held in the second week of December 2026. 

Research Project and Role
Whole-genome doubling (WGD) gives a cell an extra copy of its entire genome. It can support specialized functions during development, but it is also common in aggressive cancers, where it can promote chromosome instability and treatment resistance. After WGD, cells must copy and maintain twice as much DNA. The replication and chromatin-maintenance machinery may not increase at the same rate, creating a potential capacity bottleneck.
Our recent work identified PAF15 as a dosage-sensitive regulator of PCNA, the sliding clamp that coordinates DNA replication and repair. PAF15 helps retain PCNA on chromatin and supports maturation of the newly copied lagging strand. Its abundance must stay within a narrow range: too little weakens replication, while excess can disrupt PCNA function (PMID: 41606318; Nature. 2026 Mar;651(8105):521-532. doi: 10.1038/s41586-025-10011-3). 
Building on this work, the PhD project will investigate whether whole-genome doubling creates capacity limits in the machinery that copies and maintains the genome in non-transformed cells, cancer cells and mouse embryonic stem cells, how cells adapt to these limits, and whether the resulting dependencies could provide opportunities to target cancer cells.

The project combines quantitative cell biology, genome engineering and biochemical approaches. Methods will include quantitative image-based cytometry (QIBC), live-cell imaging, super-resolution microscopy, DNA fibre assays, CRISPR-based perturbation, stem-cell culture and differentiation, and chromatin-resolved mass spectrometry.
You will work closely with researchers in the Somyajit group and collaborators at the Department of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology. SDU provides an international and interdisciplinary research environment with advanced facilities for bioimaging, cell biology, sequencing, flow cytometry, mass spectrometry and metabolomics.

The Somyajit group is located at the Department of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology, SDU. The department constitutes an international, ambitious, highly dynamic, and well-equipped working environment with state-of-the-art facilities for advanced bioimaging, quantitative mechanistic cell biology, next generation sequencing, single-cell transcriptomics, flow cytometry, mass spectrometry, metabolomics, and transgenic mouse work. Strategic research alliances exist with Odense University Hospital (OUH).

Qualifications/requirements
We are looking for highly motivated, dedicated, and ambitious candidates with:

• 
A master’s degree in Life Science, preferable Molecular Biology, Cell Biology, Biomedicine (the 5+3 program). 

• 
Curious mind-set with a strong interest in fundamental Cell cycle, DNA replication and Genome integrity.

• 
Relevant laboratory experience in quantitative imaging and genome editing.

• 
Know-how in Genome integrity field, stem cell culture, light microscopy, bioinformatics will be considered an advantage.

• 
Strong communication and collaborative skills and an interest in working in an interdisciplinary environment.

• 
Proficiency in spoken and written English.

Requirements and programme structure
PhD candidates follow an individual PhD plan including course work, conference participation, and teaching. One semester is typically spent at another research institution - often abroad. The scholarship carries a monthly salary including pension plus office facilities and financial support for conference travels and research visits abroad. 

Application deadline: 8. December 2026 at 23:59 hours local Danish time
Please see the full call, including how to apply, on www.sdu.dk

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral position in Leptin Gene Regulation and Adipocyte Biology
jobs.description:
The Mandrup group invites applications from outstanding candidates for a Postdoctoral position in our group based at the Functional Genomics & Metabolism Research Unit, Department of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology, University of Southern Denmark. The position is offered for a duration of up to three years and will be available from January 1, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter. 

Project and Research Environment
The Postdoctoral Fellow will work on a project focusing on the molecular mechanisms regulating human leptin (LEP) gene expression in adipocytes. The aim is to identify the cis-regulatory elements, transcription factors, and signaling pathways controlling LEP expression during adipocyte differentiation and in mature adipocytes, and to understand how chromatin architecture and physiological signals are integrated to regulate leptin production. To address these questions, the project combines complementary, state-of-the-art approaches, including:

• 
Chromatin conformation analyses (e.g., Region-Capture Micro-C, Capture-C, and related approaches)

• 
Epigenomic profiling (e.g., ATAC-seq, CUT&Tag, and DynaTag)

• 
Genome editing and perturbation approaches (e.g., CRISPRi, CRISPR/Cas9, and siRNA-mediated knockdown)

• 
Transcriptomic and multi-omics analyses

• 
Computational modelling of gene regulatory networks and integration with clinical and physiological data

The project is embedded in an interdisciplinary research environment that combines molecular biology, functional genomics, computational biology, and translational studies in primary human adipocytes.

Job Description
The Postdoctoral fellow will drive experimental activities and contribute to the scientific development of the project. The position requires both independent work and close collaboration within the research group.
Key responsibilities include:

• 
Designing and conducting experiments investigating the regulation of human leptin (LEP) gene expression

• 
Generating and analyzing transcriptomic, epigenomic, and chromatin conformation datasets

• 
Integrating multi-omics, physiological, and clinical data to identify regulatory networks governing leptin expression

• 
Implementing and optimizing advanced molecular, genomic, and computational methods in adipocyte model systems and primary human adipocytes

In addition, the candidate will:

• 
Contribute to supervision and mentoring of students

• 
Participate in preparation of scientific publications and dissemination of results

• 
Actively contribute to a collaborative, ambitious, and supportive research environment

Qualifications
We are seeking a highly motivated candidate with a strong postdoctoral research profile and expertise in functional genomics and the molecular regulation of gene expression.
Required qualifications:

• 
A PhD in molecular biology, genomics, biochemistry, or a related field

• 
Strong background and experimental skills in molecular biology, functional genomics, and transcriptional regulation

• 
Ability to independently drive research projects

• 
Strong collaborative and communication skills

• 
Proficiency in spoken and written English

In addition, the following qualifications are relevant but not required: 

• 
Hands-on experience with adipocyte biology, metabolic research, or cellular differentiation systems

• 
Experience with chromatin conformation methods (e.g., Capture-C, Micro-C, Hi-C, or related approaches)

• 
Experience with epigenomic and transcriptomic techniques (e.g., ATAC-seq, CUT&Tag, RNA-seq, or related sequencing-based assays)

• 
Experience with analysis and integration of multi-omics datasets

• 
Experience with computational biology, bioinformatics pipelines, and R for data analysis and visualization

• 
Hands-on experience with genome editing and gene perturbation technologies (e.g., CRISPR/Cas9, CRISPRi, or RNA interference)

We offer

• 
A position in a focused, externally funded research project at the forefront of chromatin biology research

• 
Access to state-of-the-art infrastructure within genomics, imaging, and molecular biology

• 
An international, highly collaborative, and dynamic research environment

• 
Strong support for scientific development and career progression

• 
Competitive salary and comprehensive social benefits

The Mandrup Group
The Mandrup Group has a long-standing interest in the detailed molecular mechanisms governing transcriptional control of adipocyte differentiation. We apply a variety of sequencing-based, computational, and molecular technologies, combined with loss- and gain-of-function strategies to study the mechanisms and role of the 3D chromatin architecture, the crosstalk between enhancers in enhancer communities and the role of specific transcription factors.
You will work closely together with other postdoctoral fellows and PhD students in the group, and you will also be expected to collaborate with colleagues in the Center of Excellence in Functional Genomics and Tissue Plasticity (ATLAS) and Center of Adipocyte Signaling (ADIPOSIGN), both directed by Susanne Mandrup. Furthermore, you will be able to benefit from the many international collaborations of our group.

The Functional Genomics & Metabolism Research Unit 
The Mandrup Group is located in the Functional Genomics & Metabolism Research Unit at the Department of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology, SDU. The research unit currently hosts eight independent research groups focusing on how specific cell types regulate gene expression and how this affects the development and function of cells and tissues. Thus, our research aims to better understand how genes regulate human physiology and diseases such as obesity, fatty liver disease, cancer, and diabetes. The research unit constitutes an international, ambitious, highly dynamic, and well-equipped working environment. The unit and the department have state-of-the-art facilities for next-generation sequencing, single-cell transcriptomics and epigenomics, flow cytometry, mass spectrometry, metabolomics, bioimaging, cell culture, and dietary intervention and transgenic mouse models. The unit maintains strategic research alliances with Odense University Hospital (OUH). This provides a highly stimulating research environment with numerous opportunities for learning and developing new ideas.

jobs.occupation: Associate Professor at the Department of Public Health
jobs.description:
The Department of Public Health at the Faculty of Health, Aarhus University, invites applications for a full-time position as Associate Professor with a research and teaching profile in the area of complex interventions. The expected starting date is February 1st, 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. The position is a three-year position that expires on January 31st, 2030.

About the Department
The Department of Public Health is a research-intensive environment dedicated to advancing scientific knowledge and developing applied solutions to major public health challenges. Our research spans theoretical, basic, and applied sciences, with the shared ambition of generating impactful knowledge and improving population health. Academic excellence is at the core of everything we do. We are committed to conducting rigorous and innovative research and delivering high-quality teaching. We teach across public health, sport science, health science, nursing science, related methodological disciplines, and the medical degree programme.

Rooted in our respective disciplines, we foster interdisciplinary collaboration to strengthen research, education and innovation. We are equally committed to cultivating a healthy and supportive workplace characterised by open dialogue, mutual respect and an informal atmosphere. We believe that academic excellence and personal well-being are mutually reinforcing and essential to long-term success.
You can read more about the department here and about the faculty here.

Your job responsibilities
As an Associate Professor of Public Health, you will contribute to the department’s research and teaching environment and to the faculty’s overall research strategy. You will contribute to the development of the department both individually and in collaboration with others via your research of high international quality. You ensure that your teaching maintains a high academic and didactic standard. You possess professional collaborative skills and a broad academic network which you are able to bring into play in your contribution to the academic development of Aarhus University and its profile both nationally and internationally. 

Your primary responsibilities will include:

• Conducting and publishing research of high international quality, including in leading journals and with leading publishers within your field.
• Developing your research profile and contributing to the department's objectives, including raising research external funding for your research projects.
• Teaching and supervising students at Bachelor's and Master's level and contributing to the continued development of innovative teaching activities.
• Participating in the supervision of PhD students and contributing to the faculty's PhD courses.
• Disseminating research findings to academic audiences, stakeholders, and the wider public.
You will report to the Head of Department Michael Baggesen Klitagaard.

Your competences 
You have established yourself as a recognised researcher within your field and can document research and teaching qualifications at a high international level. You have a well-developed international network, experience in attracting significant external research funding from national and international funding bodies, and clear potential and motivation to establish yourself as a research leader, to establish your own research group, and to consolidate an independent research agenda. In the assessment process, emphasis will be placed on experience gained through employment, visiting appointments, or extended research stays at recognised universities or research institutions outside the candidate's primary institution.

Your personal qualities include the ability to build trust-based relationships with colleagues, students, and external partners. As a teacher, you communicate current and relevant knowledge in a clear, engaging, and inspiring manner. As a supervisor, you are professional, inclusive, and supportive. You value collaboration and contribute positively to the collegial culture that characterises the Department of Public Health, the Faculty of Health Sciences, and Aarhus University more broadly. You are motivated to contribute to the department's continued development and to help maintain an inclusive, supportive, and high-performing work environment.

We expect you to be fluent in oral and written English. International applicants are expected to learn Danish, and Aarhus University arranges Danish teaching. 

In order to be assessed as qualified for an Associate Professor position, you must meet these academic criteria.

Shortlisting will be applied as part of the assessment process.

Questions about the position
If you have any questions about the position, please contact Head of Department Michael Baggesen Klitgaard tel.: (+45) 4022 7649. Your place of work will be the Department of Public Health, DK-8000 Aarhus C, Denmark. 

Terms of employment
• Appointment as an associate professor requires research and teaching qualifications at the level that can be achieved through the satisfactory completion of a period of appointment as an assistant professor, but may also be obtained in other ways.
• The applicant is required to have completed a university pedagogical programme or an equivalent programme.
• Further information on the appointment procedure can be found in the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities.
• The appointment is in accordance with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (Akademikerne).
• Remuneration is in accordance with the above, and the Salary agreement catalogue for staff at Health.
• The yearly base salary for a fulltime associate professor is DKK 706.233,06 (including a position related supplement, a pre-agreed associate professor supplememt and pension (18.07%)). Additional supplement(s) can be negotiated dependent on experience, special qualifications and performance of special functions. Authorisation supplement(s) will be granted, if relevant for the position. Your local eligible trade union representative at Aarhus University negotiates your salary on your behalf.
• Researchers recruited from abroad are offered a special researcher tax scheme with a lower tax rate.
• Travel and moving expenses may be covered according to the employee in question and, to a limited extent, the accompanying family.
• Further information on qualification requirements and job description can be found in the Ministerial order on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities.
Application
Your application must include the following:

• Motivated application
• Curriculum Vitae
• Diploma
• Template for applicant - associate professor
• A list of publications
• A teaching portfolio. We refer to Guideline on the use of teaching portfolios
• The five publications stated as the most important in the 'Template for applicant - associate professor' must be submitted
• Research plan, which is part of the 'Template to applicant - associate professor' can be uploaded separately (optional)
• Coauthor statement(s) can be uploaded (optional)
• References/recommendations can be uploaded separately in the e-recruitment system (optional)
We refer to the faculty’s Guidelines for applicants.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

International applicant?
Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including assistance with relocation and career counselling to expat partners. Please find more information about the International Staff Office and the range of services here.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

About Aarhus University

Aarhus University is an academically diverse and research-intensive university with a strong commitment to high-quality research and education and the development of society nationally and globally. The university offers an inspiring research and teaching environment for its 37,500 students, including PhD students, and has 9,000 employees (full-time equivalents) and an annual revenue of EUR 1.2 billion. Learn more at international.au.dk

jobs.occupation: Laboratory Technician at NIVI Research Center
jobs.description:
The research group of Associate Professor Stephan Brouwer is looking for an engaged laboratory technician with experience in molecular biology, immunology, mammalian cell culture, and preferably with experience in BSL2/GMO-2 practices and research. The position is permanent and open for appointment from 1 March 2027.

  About us
 The Novo Nordisk Foundation Initiative for Vaccines and Immunity (NIVI), launched in December 2023, has a unique mission to harness airway immunity through innovative vaccine research and development to prevent airborne epidemics. NIVI has two parts:

  · NIVI Research Center (NIVI-R): A state-of-the-art research center anchored to the University of Copenhagen, Department of Immunology and Microbiology (www.isim.ku.dk).

  · NIVI Development (NIVI-D): A company that focuses on translational sciences and advancing vaccine development.

  NIVI-R conducts scientific research, while NIVI-D works to quickly turn that research into new vaccine candidates. NIVI-D accelerates clinical trials (phases 1 and 2) and ensures a smooth transition to partners for later stages of development.

  By connecting science, innovation, clinical trials, regulatory processes, and product development, NIVI aims to streamline the journey from research to real-world vaccines.

  Your tasks
 As part of a newly established research center, you will contribute to the setup and development of a completely new laboratory. This will include assisting with laboratory organization, implementation of workflows and procedures, inventory management systems, and establishing best practices for laboratory operations. You will work closely with the other laboratory technicians and scientific staff within NIVI-R to create a well-functioning research environment while helping to ensure the smooth day-to-day operation of the laboratory.

  As the laboratory technician, you will carry out several routine laboratory tasks; including maintenance of mammalian cell lines, molecular biology protocols (e.g., Protein purification, IVT-mRNA synthesis, DNA and RNA extraction/purification, Western-Blot/SDS-PAGE, PCR, qRT-PCR), Immunological assays (e.g. ELISA/Luminex, Neutralization assay, Flow cytometry), preparation of laboratory reagents, and other daily lab routines.

  You will also participate in various research projects that involve the development of vaccines and the characterization of vaccine responses, and close collaboration with the group’s scientists.

  The following will also be part of the role:

   	
• Documenting all laboratory work accurately using electronic lab notebooks. 	
• Monitoring laboratory stocks and ensuring timely replenishment. 	
• Organizing the laboratory and related space to be a clean, safe, and functional environment.   Profile
 Essential experience and skills:

  We are looking for someone with experience in molecular biology techniques (e.g., PCR, western blot, DNA/RNA work), mammalian cell culture (e.g., maintaining, freezing, and characterizing cell lines), and immunologic assays (ELISA, Flowcytometry).

   	
• A degree as a laboratory technician (Academy Profession degree or similar) is required. 	
• You must be good at working independently and organized, and be self-motivated 	
• Have good interpersonal and communication skills, both in Danish and English; spoken and written   Desirable experience and skills:

   	
• Experience with laboratory research in (BSL-2/GMO-2) labs. 	
• Experience with immunological assays: Proficiency in techniques such as ELISA/Luminex, Western Blotting, or Flow Cytometry (FACS) to support vaccine efficacy studies. 	
• Experience with cell culture, routine mycoplasma testing, and the validation of sterile reagents and media. 	
• Experience in animal research (active FELSA/ABD certification).   Terms of salary and employment
 Your employment will be at NIVI Research Center, Department of Immunology and Microbiology, University of Copenhagen. The position is full-time (37 hours per week), permanent, and is open for appointment from 1 March 2027.

  Employment as laboratory technician will be in accordance with the agreement between the Danish Ministry of Finance and OAO/HK STAT. The position is placed in salary group 4.

  Depending on qualifications a supplement may be negotiated.

  Question
 For further information please contact Stephan Brouwer: stephan.brouwer@sund.ku.dk

  Application
 Please submit your application in English by clicking "Apply for position" below. 

  The application should consist of the following:

   	
• Letter of application/motivation (max 1 page) 	
• Your CV incl. education, a list of laboratory skills/techniques, previous employments, language skills and other relevant skills 	
• Copy of relevant certificate/diploma   Deadline for application is 9 December 2027, 23.59 CET.
 We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements.

   

  University of Copenhagen wish to reflect the diversity of society and welcome applications from all qualified candidates regardless of age, disability, gender, nationality, race, religion or sexual orientation. Appointment will be based on merit alone

jobs.occupation: Postdoc in Cognitive Computational Neuroscience and Human Movement Perception
jobs.description:
The Department of Psychology invites applications for a postdoctoral position in Cognitive Computational Neuroscience and Human Movement Perception by 1 March 2027 or after agreement.

  The position is a fixed-term position for 30 months/2.5 years.
 
 Introduction
 The postdoc will be part of a project entitled "Mapping Experience of Action: Redefining Theories of Consciousness" funded by the Independent Research Fund Denmark. The project is headed by Professor Thor Grünbaum and Associate Professor in Cognitive Psychology Mark Schram Christensen Department of Psychology, University of Copenhagen.

  This interdisciplinary project develops a novel scientific approach to the study of consciousness by investigating conscious experiences of movement. Combining psychophysical experiments, computational modelling, and philosophical analysis, it examines how bodily and neural signals contribute to movement awareness. The project aims to advance our understanding of consciousness and critically evaluate leading neuroscientific theories of conscious experience.

  Applicants are asked to develop a short project description for the postdoc. It is critical that applicants are able to situate their project and research plan within the framework of the overall project. It is a requirement that applicants request from Associate Professor Mark Schram Christensen (markc@psy.ku.dk) the original project proposal prior to submitting the application.

  Candidates with various background may be considered for the position. Examples of relevant backgrounds are PhDs in cognitive (neuro)science, computational neuroscience, cognitive modelling, biomedical engineering, sports science with a focus on behavioural neuroscience, or similar. The candidates are expected to have strong skills in cognitive modelling, experimental design, data handling and data analysis documented in relevant scientific publications.

  The postdoc will be working in close collaboration with the other project members which has academic backgrounds in cognitive neuroscience and philosophy, and student assistants with background in Cognitive Data Science.  The position will be placed in the Cognition, Intention and Action research group, part of the Section for Cognition and Brain Sciences, Department of Psychology.  It is expected that the successful candidate will be present, part of the team, and take part in the activities in the Lab on a daily basis.
 
 Duties and Responsibilities
 The primary focus of the postdoctoral position will be on research within the main project. However, a certain amount of teaching obligations may be required. Additional tasks beyond research and teaching may also be considered, but to a limited extent. The university will determine the final scope of the various responsibilities, and the emphasis may vary over time.
 
 Qualification Requirements 
 Appointment as a postdoctoral researcher requires research qualifications at a level at least equivalent to those obtained through the satisfactory completion of a PhD programme within the relevant field.

  Strong skills in data handling and analysis are crucial, and experience with cognitive/computational modelling within human behavioural science or neuroscience is key to the content of the project. 

  You can find further information about the qualification requirements for postdoctoral positions here: Ministerial Order on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities (In Danish only).

  You can also find further information about the postdoctoral position on our English webpage on career paths for early‑career researchers at the University of Copenhagen: Career at The University of Copenhagen.
 
 Strategy of the Faculty of the Social Sciences
 The Department of Psychology is part of the Faculty of the Social Sciences. The faculty is a successful academic community that strives to put knowledge into action by:

  Engaging partners in the co-creation of knowledge, learning and social change.

  Empowering our students to become reflective and responsible citizens who have the vision, the knowledge and the competences to change society for the better.

  Energising global, European and Danish communities of knowledge by innovating research methodologies and by research findings with impact.

  For more on the faculty’s strategy, please see: Strategy for the Faculty of Social Science.
 
 Assessment Criteria
 Applicants will primarily be assessed in relation to their research qualifications, including their publications, ability to conduct independent research and participate in research collaborations, and their experience of research management. In addition, the applicant’s research plan and research potential will be assessed in relation to the overall project described above.

  Teaching qualifications are not a requirement.
 
 Application
 Please submit your application online. To apply, please click on the “Apply now” icon at the bottom of this page. The application must be written in English, and include the following attachments in PDF or Word format:

   	
• CV (max. 3 pages) 	
• Cover letter including the preferred starting date (max. 1 page) 	
• Documentation of qualifications (exam certificates and PhD diploma) 	
• Complete publication list (attached publications must be marked with an asterisk). The list must be structured systematically and divided into the following categories: 	 		
• Peer-reviewed publications: 		
• Monographs and anthologies 		
• Articles in journals 		
• Book chapters/anthology contributions, etc. 		
• Non-peer-reviewed publications: 		
• Publications disseminating research findings, etc.
 		  	 	 	
• You can attach a maximum of 3 publications. The publication dates must be clearly marked on the list. The selected publications must be uploaded as attachments and numbered 1-3.
 	  	
• A short project description (max. 2 pages). 	 		
• The description should outline your ideas for the postdoc project situated in the state-of-the-art research in the field of the project. It should include your proposals for specific types of experimental and modelling approaches that you envision to contribute with to the project. The description must not exceed 2 standard pages, corresponding to approx. 4,800 characters (including title, punctuation, figures, footnotes and references, but excluding bibliography). A substantial breach of this will result in the application being excluded from consideration.
 		  	 	 	
• Research plan (max. 2 pages) 	 		
• The plan should include a brief account of previous research, current research projects, and a forward-looking outline of planned research contribution over the coming years. This may include specific references to the project proposals funded by Independent Research Foundation Denmark, and how the candidate expect to contribute to the project at large. 	 	   
 Salary and Terms of Employment
 Terms of appointment and salary will be in accordance with an agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC). The salary range for postdoctoral positions starts at DKK 39,000/approximately EUR 5,100 + an 18.07 % pension contribution. It is possible to negotiate salary supplements on an annual basis.
 
 Recruitment Process
 After the application deadline, the Head of Department will consider advice from the appointment committee and select applicants for assessment. All applicants will be notified whether they have been shortlisted. The Head of Department will set up an expert assessment committee to assess the shortlisted applications. The selected applicants will be informed who is serving on the committee. Each shortlisted applicant will be offered the opportunity to comment on the committee’s assessment before the appointment is announced.

  You can find further information on our recruitment process at: Recruitment process.
 
 International Applicant?
 The University of Copenhagen offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including support before and during your relocation and career counselling to expat partners. Please find more information about our services at: For international researchers at the University of Copenhagen.
 
 An Equal Opportunity Workplace
 The University of Copenhagen is committed in its pursuit of academic excellence to equality of opportunity and to creating an inclusive working environment and therefore encourages all qualified candidates to apply, regardless of personal background, gender, sexual orientation, age, disability, ethnicity etc. To learn more about our diverse workplace and our participation in the HRS4R HR Excellence in Research, please visit HR Excellence in Research.
 
 Contact Information
 For additional information about the position, please contact Associate Professor Mark Schram Christensen at email markc@psy.ku.dk or phone +45-3532 2448.

  For more Information about the recruitment process, please contact HR South at hr-soendre@adm.ku.dk. Please refer to ID number: 211-2675/26-2I

  The application deadline is 1 December 2026 at 23:59 CET.

  Any applications or additional material submitted after the deadline will not be considered. However, changes may be made to the submitted application right up until the deadline.

jobs.occupation: Regional Director – Nordics & Baltics | Successful International Group
jobs.description:
About the Company

Our client is a successful international distributor of specialty chemicals, with operations across a number of international markets and a presence in more than 20 countries.

The group holds a strong international position and is currently working to strengthen its presence and drive further growth in the Nordics and Baltics.

You will become a pivotal part of an international organization, with excellent opportunities to influence development and shape the direction of future commercial growth.

About the Position

As Regional Director – Nordics & Baltics, you will have overall responsibility for the business unit's development, performance, and future direction in the region.

Your primary task will be to set the strategic direction and ensure the continuous development of the business. You will play a central role in translating the group's ambitions into concrete goals and results, as well as creating the organizational and commercial framework for future growth.

In close collaboration with the Sales Director, you will develop and implement the strategy for the region and ensure progress through clear leadership, prioritization, and strong cooperation with the rest of the organization.

You will establish direction and engagement within the organization, develop leaders and employees, and ensure that the right competencies and resources are brought into play. The role requires the ability to deliver results through others while maintaining a strategic overview and an understanding of the business's commercial opportunities.

Your Primary Responsibilities

• Develop leaders and employees with a focus on competencies, engagement, accountability, and collaboration.
• Translate the group's overall ambitions into concrete strategies, goals, and action plans.
• Support a company culture characterized by initiative, ownership, openness, and continuous development.
About You

You have leadership experience and a strong strategic understanding. You possess the ability to gain commitment, set direction, and develop an organization through clear leadership, involvement, and trust.

You do not necessarily need to have held a director-level position previously. The most important thing is that you have the ambition, the strategic overview, and the ability to take overall responsibility for a business unit's development and results.

We imagine that you:

• Have experience in commercial leadership and organizational development, including developing and implementing strategies and translating them into concrete goals and results.
• Are a clear leader who sets direction, builds engagement, and ensures progress.
• Thrive with overall responsibility and are able to maintain both the strategic overview and an understanding of the organization's daily operations.
• Are a modern leader who believes in freedom with responsibility and is motivated by coaching and facilitating rather than micromanaging.
• Have experience in developing people and achieving results through others.
• Possess a good financial understanding and the ability to make decisions on a sound strategic and financial basis.
• Have experience from the specialty chemicals industry or related sectors. This will be considered an advantage.
• Communicate effortlessly in both Danish and English. Additional language skills are an advantage.
What Is Offered

• A central leadership position with responsibility for an international business unit that is part of a successful global group.
• A commercial mandate with the opportunity to influence strategy and organization and leave a clear mark on the development of the Nordics and Baltics.
• A dynamic working environment combining strategic responsibility, leadership, and organizational development.
• Business travel in connection with the development of the business in the Nordics and Baltics, with significant influence over your own travel planning.

You can be based anywhere in Denmark, as there are good opportunities for remote work. If you live outside daily commuting distance, you will be expected to work from the office approximately once a week.

Application

jobs.occupation: Postdoc in computational multimodal data integration for crop stress regulatory networks
jobs.description:
The Department of Plant and Environmental Sciences (PLEN) invites applications for a postdoctoral position in computational biology, focused on the integration of multimodal single-cell, epigenomic and literature-derived data into gene regulatory networks. The position is financed by the Novo Nordisk Foundation through the Ascending Investigator grant “Accelerating crop resilience with AI-enabled gene function prediction and stress regulatory networks” (NNF26OC0113093).

  The position is for 3 years. Start date is 1 March 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

  The project  Climate-driven heat and drought increasingly destabilise crop yields, yet the gene regulatory networks that govern stress responses in crops remain poorly resolved, because they have mostly been measured in whole organs. This programme will resolve them at the level of individual cell types and their cis-regulatory elements, in four major Nordic crops – rapeseed, potato, wheat and barley – under heat, drought and the two combined.

  The postdoc is the computational integrator of the grant: the person who turns the data the grant generates into regulatory networks. The single-cell RNA-seq and ATAC-seq data are generated by a PhD student and a technician on the group’s 10x Genomics platform; your job begins when the sequencing reads arrive. This is a purely computational position – no wet-lab work is involved. Concretely, you will:

   	
• Build the analysis backbone for the single-cell stress atlases: quality control, doublet and ambient-RNA handling, integration across four species, three stress conditions, three organs and three time points, and cell-type annotation using conserved markers – with pipelines the PhD students can run and extend. 	
• Integrate the modalities into gene regulatory networks. Infer transcription factor–target relationships by extending the group’s TEA-GCN method to single-cell data; identify cis-regulatory elements from accessible chromatin using known motifs, de novo motif discovery, convolutional neural networks and DNA language models; and link the two into TF–CRE–target triplets. Benchmark against SCENIC+, MAESTRO and related frameworks and adopt what works. 	
• Rank regulatory relationships by conservation across the four crops to obtain a high-confidence core, and develop the comparative methods this needs. 	
• Connect the networks to the rest of the grant’s work: to the group’s literature-derived knowledge graph and gene-function predictions, and to the open web platform through which the grant’s data, models and predictions are shared, so that regulators and targets can be prioritised for validation in rapeseed with traceable evidence. 	
• Co-supervise and train the PhD students and master’s students on the computational side, and help build the group’s single-cell and multi-omics analysis capacity.   Who are we looking for?  You hold a PhD in bioinformatics, computational biology, genomics, plant molecular biology or a related field, and you have analysed single-cell or other high-dimensional omics data independently. We are looking for a computational scientist who can take raw multimodal data through to a defensible biological claim, and who is comfortable working alongside the experimentalists who generate the data.

  Essential:

   	
• A PhD (or a thesis submitted by the start date) in a relevant field 	
• Documented experience with the analysis of single-cell RNA-seq and/or single-cell ATAC-seq data, or with comparable multimodal genomic data 	
• Strong programming proficiency in Python or R, and experience building reproducible analysis workflows (e.g. Snakemake/Nextflow, version control, containers) 	
• A publication record demonstrating independent scientific contribution 	
• Excellent written and spoken English   Advantageous:

   	
• Experience with gene regulatory network inference, motif analysis or cis-regulatory element prediction 	
• Experience with deep-learning models of regulatory sequence (CNNs, DNA language models) or with graph-based methods 	
• Experience with comparative or cross-species analysis of transcriptomic data 	
• Experience with plant abiotic stress biology or with crop species 	
• Experience co-supervising students   Our group and research – and what do we offer?  The Mutwil group at PLEN works at the interface of comparative and evolutionary plant biology and AI-driven biological discovery. We build large cross-species gene expression atlases, comparative co-expression networks and knowledge graphs, and we use machine learning and large language models to turn the plant literature and omics archives into testable hypotheses. The group comprises several PhD students, postdocs and master’s students, and maintains a portfolio of widely used community resources under the .plant.tools domain, including PlantConnectome, CoNekt, diurnal.plant.tools and evorepro.plant.tools.

  The postdoc will work closely with the two PhD students funded by the same grant (literature-derived knowledge graphs and gene-function prediction; single-cell stress experiments) and with collaborators Prof. Ryan Lister (University of Western Australia, multimodal single-cell genomics) and Prof. Zoran Nikoloski (University of Potsdam, regulatory network inference).

  The group is part of the Department of Plant and Environmental Sciences (PLEN), Faculty of Science, University of Copenhagen. We are located on the Frederiksberg Campus in Copenhagen. We offer creative and stimulating working conditions in a dynamic and international research environment. Computational resources include a 196-thread/1 TB RAM workstation and guaranteed GPU access through LUMI and uCloud.

  Inquiries about the position can be made to Associate Professor Marek Mutwil, mutwil@plen.ku.dk.

  Terms of employment  The position is covered by the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff. Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Ministry of Taxation and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State. Negotiation for salary supplement is possible.

  Application procedure  Your application, in English, must be submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below. Please include:

   	
• Motivated letter of application (max. one page) 	
• Curriculum vitae, including information about your education, experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position 	
• Diplomas (Master and PhD degree or equivalent). If the PhD is not yet awarded, documentation of the expected date of the defence 	
• Complete publication list 	
• Separate reproductions of up to three particularly relevant papers 	
• Research statement (max. two pages) describing your previous work and how you would approach the multimodal integration and network-inference tasks described above 	
• Names and contact details of two or three references   The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

  Application deadline: The deadline for applications is 31 January 2027, 23:59 GMT +1.

  We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements.

  The further process  After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorised recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the Interview Committee. Afterwards an assessment committee will be appointed to evaluate the selected applications. The applicants will be notified of the composition of the committee and the final selection of a successful candidate will be made by the Head of Department, based on the recommendations of the assessment committee and the interview committee. The applicant will be assessed according to the Ministerial Order no. 242 of 13 March 2012 on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities.

  You can read about the recruitment process at http://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/.

  Interviews with selected candidates are expected to be held in February 2027.
